The drawing shows a 2,3-dihydrobenzofuran core with these substituents:

- **C2:** two phenyl groups (Ph, Ph).
- **C3:** an NH group attached to a tert-octyl group, C(Me)2–CH2–C(Me)3 (1,1,3,3-tetramethylbutyl).
- **C4 of the benzofuran:** Cl, on the benzene carbon next to C3a.

Ring connectivity: the benzene ring carries Cl on the carbon adjacent to C3a. C3a is bonded to C3, and C7a is bonded to O.

SMILES, written from C3:
- C3: `C(NC(C)(C)CC(C)(C)C)`
- C2: `C(c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)`
- O, then C7a (`c2...`), C7, C6, C5, C4(Cl), C3a.

Full SMILES: `CC(C)(C)CC(C)(C)NC1C(c2ccccc2)(c2ccccc2)Oc2cccc(Cl)c21`

Check of the benzo ring: `Oc2cccc(Cl)c21` gives C7a (the c2 bonded to O), then C7, C6, C5, then C4 bearing Cl, then C3a closing both rings. This is correct.

The drawing uses plain bonds at C3, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)CC(C)(C)NC1C(c2ccccc2)(c2ccccc2)Oc2cccc(Cl)c21
